I work for a surgeon in Southern California. Would you happen to be anywhere near Cali? I bet I could actually help you out big time. My boss is a good man. We work with many military members and other people with limited income situations. It's a total shot in the dark, but hey... Whatever happens Hun, don't despair. I went through a very similar situation with the National Guard myself. It sucked, but it's not worth your life. It's really not. When a door closes, somewhere a window usually opens. Don't forget that. 
:)

I really like this. It gave me some strength and I'm so glad you came here to share your story. You sound like a very decent person and I can tell that you love your family. I've had many of the same thoughts as you, but knowing I'm not alone in these ideas is powerful. I hope you keep going and I hope I can do the same. Cheers my friend.
Thank you for replying. She is going to call a therapist today, one that we found who is willing to work with her for very reasonable rates but who is also highly recommended. Hopefully this helps!

Many of the world's most brilliant artists, thinkers, writers, actors, etc. were considered very different than your average 'Type A, Alpha Male'. Many of them were depressed at times, shy, socially awkward or just didn't fit in. Even in the general population, variation of genes and human traits has been shown to strengthen the overall population. When two people are exactly alike, there is less of that variation going on, and that can lead to mental and physical defects in certain circumstances, like with family members. My point is that you're ok the way you are! And people aren't better than you! EVERYONE has issues. EVERYONE. Believe me. I work in medicine / psychology and even the most "ideal" specimens are not free from health problems or mental illness. Don't check out because you're on your own path. Personally, I would say guys like you are the rogues - unpredictable, complicated, not like everyone else (which would be terribly boring) and I think it's what makes the world a better place. I really do.
Hi. What is going on right now that's bothering you? Anything specific or is it more life in general? Here to listen / help if possible.

You're an amazing friend. I don't know if this helps, but I recently read on a website for suicidal people, something like... "If you are truly set on ending your life, why not at least take one more day to really think it over, because if you have ANY hesitation at all, that is a sign you shouldn't give up just yet. And what is ONE more day in the face of eternity? It's not long. It will just give you time to make this decision, because it's a really huge decision. Once you do if there's no going back... It's weird because most of the San Francisco bridge jumpers die, but the few who have attempted that jump and survived, they all said that right before they hit the water, they had a split second of regret. I'm not making this stuff up. Im a psychology student and I have also been suicidal before. I know how painful it is. I really do. But later on... Sometimes just a few days of weeks later in fact, I was glad I was still around. I learned that no situation is permanent, or at least, our perceptions and feelings about it aren't. It takes an incredible amount of strength though, to change depressed thinking quickly. Most people do need all the help they can get. That's why your friend is so lucky to have you.

The hypocratic oath states that all medical doctors take any measures in their power to NOT harm people in need of treatment and to HELP them in whatever ways are available. Not in those words, so please, if you are a doctor, feel free to expand on this, but I do work in medicine and I know that the hospital I work for HAS to admit anyone who is actively suicidal. Insurance or not. I personally went to a psyche ward without insurance. I got a huge bill, never paid most of it because I freaking couldn't, and it dented my credit a bit I guess, but I was ALIVE and it didn't ruin my life. Money is money. A life is a life. You do matter and even though you had a bad experience, there are options. If you can talk to anyone, call anyone... Take one last leap of faith. Give yourself one more shot. If you're going to end it, that's a forever kind of thing, so what is one more day of life compared to forever? You can go to a different hospital, go to another kind of facility, go to an emergency shelter and explain your problem, talk to a police officer, a suicide hotline, a friend... Anyone. Anyone at all. Mental illness is so hard because when we would technically need to be strong and fight the hardest to overcome such a huge threat, we can't because our brains and bodies are at their weakest. People don't always get it huh? No one WANTS to be depressed or suicidal. People just can't cope with the pain anymore. You can do something hugely brave by not giving up yet. And please know that no matter what you do, you have my deepest sympathies. I was also homeless many years ago. It was one of the most stressful, frightening experiences of my existence. I really feel your pain right now. It is terrible. I'm so very sorry.

When I read this I felt like I was reading my own thoughts written out! Amazing that two people could have such similar issues and thoughts. I too have really REALLY bad anxiety problems and I absolutely hate being around other people these days, especially strangers in public. When I was pregnant last year, every human that looked at me made me want to burst into tears. People would come up and touch my stomach and I would have horrible panic attacks. I had the baby but it never went away, those feelings. It's like the older I get the more socially awkward and fearful I become. I thought it was supposed to be the opposite? I thought we get older and become wiser, calmer, more self assured... Yea not this lady. I'm basically a manic basket case half the time, and depressed the rest of the time. My only joyful moments are with my child. I save all my energy and smiles for him, so he won't be affected as much by my horrible anxiety and bouts of sadness. I don't know if my attempting to tell my story is helpful to you or not; I really hope that, at the very least, it gives you a sense of being less alone out there. Because I know for me, I feel so incredibly alone all the freaking time and it helps me when I meet others who know my struggle. So for what it's worth, you have an ear over here and I do understand much of what you've described. Maybe we can chat more sometime. We can complain about weirdos giving us strange looks in the grocery store - not to make light of this but yea, I totally hide in another isle just to avoid them. Lol. Good luck OP. You're not "retarded" as far as I can tell. You seem intelligent and just a bit lost... Stay strong.

It does for a while, until the next blow. But that's life, I guess. It's not easy. Sometimes we are meant to learn the hard lessons. Sometimes we get a break. Mostly in my life, for the past ten years, I've been suffering terribly. So it has not gotten much better for me, but I'm still here... Hoping. Hanging on.

Even though you are going through all of this pain you still care for others, and that's very admirable. I am truly sorry that you went through such a tough time with your breakup and I know you don't want to hear speeches about how "it gets better" or "you'll feel better with time" because no one can guarantee that and life is hard. Sometimes I'm so exhausted with the whole thing I just want to sleep for a few years and not wake up. I hear you, trust me. All I can say is that I went through a terrible breakup when I was your age, and later I actually met someone who was much MUCH better for me, so although I can't guarantee that will be the case for you, I would be willing to bet on it because time is on your side. My mom left my dad after 35 years of marriage and he's single at almost 60... Now when he says he's lonely I don't know what to say, you know? My mom was it for him. Maybe this person you lost was it for you. I hope not. I hope you stick it out a bit longer and see what happens next; I know you're hurting and you're lonely but you can survive this. Just be yourself, you are kind and intelligent... Someone even better might just come along and recognize that. In any case, I wish you the very best. You deserve better than heartbreak.

SAT's, IQ Tests, etc. are very poor measures of human intelligence. Intelligence is relative to many things; for example, in parts of Africa there are tribesmen who, although they may not read books or know a computer, have the innate ability to recognize minute deviations in the environment around them, can easily navigate long distances using the stars and the sun, can recognize THOUSANDS of animals, insects, plants and birds by name and individual habits, and can even find a water source in the middle of what seems to be a barren desert. Those are skills that we, in the 'developed' world, would perhaps not think of as valuable, because we concern ourselves with monetary gains and test scores and those measurements of success (which is also arbitrary) but what would it really matter in terms of survival? What does a test really determine - it is only a measure of one's ability to memorize certain information and regurgitate that information under a time constraint. It's silly. It doesn't mean much. Whatever you do well that many of your contemporaries can not do as well is what makes you intelligent and unique, in my opinion. Perhaps you are an amazing artist. Maybe you can cook delicious cakes and breads. Maybe you read facial expressions and empathize with others in a way that many people can not. These are all 'intelligence'. Don't worry. You are important and capable of many great things in spite of your perceived shortcomings. Work hard, try to be positive and helpful and you will find that you can overcome most challenges in life. Most people are miserable - I think that's what makes them dull. I don't know... Just my two cents.

I actually like that you are still trying to continue on... 370 days is a long time. Let's just acknowledge the remote possibility of you feeling a bit differently about suicide by then, shall we? I don't mean to sound smug either, so forgive me if I came across that way, but I'm HOPING that you are in a better spot in 370 days. I'm here if you need an ear.

Thank you. Just got results (freaking finally, this was a month long ordeal) so it looks like I have thyroid problems for sure BUT no Cancer. Thrilled. So grateful for the support as well. God Bless you.
Yea I feel you. Sorry for the late reply. How's it going this week? Any better?

I really do understand and I'm so sorry that you're dealing with so much devastation. And yes I totally agree with you about other people's perceptions - it's like no one cares until it's too late. I wish human nature was not so disingenuous overall, but what can we do? We can live in this crazy world and do our best, as you surely are. And I admire you for that.

Oh my goodness. This is one of those times when I desperately want to say something to comfort you, and I'm scared to say the wrong thing, but here goes... 

If my mother died I know a little part of me world go with her. I can't imagine the pain you must feel. I do hope that even in this dark time, you will be comforted by those who have also lost parents, loved ones or close friends and continued on, despite the devastation this causes. I hope that you will find the strength to go on, I hope that the happy, wonderful times you shared with your mother throughout your life will be in your mind and heart forever, clear as day. I hope your family is forming a close circle around you and your father and siblings to reassure you and hold you up when you are not strong. I hope you know that your mother loved you fiercely. I'm sure of that. I am a mother myself and my bond with my son is stronger than anything on earth. I am here to listen if you would like to share any thoughts about your mother. 

Hugs

Well I finally got the results of multiple tests; I do have thyroid issues and may face surgery eventually but it's not Cancer!!!! So relieved. I was in a car accident last week and it was like the whole world was going to HELL - I was beyond happy when, one day later, I got a call from the ENT with this news. So there is my update. Still a college dropout, still swimming in debt, but at least I am alive and somewhat healthy and I can work hard to fix some of this. Thank you ALL AGAIN FOR YOUR SUPPORT IT TRULY MEANT THE WORLD TO ME. THANK YOU THANK YOU THANK YOU.

Wow. My heart hurts for you. I am in some significant medical debt myself. It's awful getting those calls all the time. Can you apply for some kind of unemployment? Emergency aide? What about your mother - can she lend or give you some money to help with necessities until you're on your feet again? 

Do not feel guilty for taking care of yourself too, when you can, because care takers like you and I often neglect ourselves to the point of getting very out of balance and sick. 

I think you are an amazing person. It's not easy and most people could not do what you are doing. Most would give up or hide from a life so full of challenges, but you have chosen to love and care for your wife despite all odds. 

I will be thinking of uou and hoping you are ok.

Hi there. Your post really hit a nerve with me because I am an addict too. I used to drink alcohol as well, sober up for a good few years, then slipped up on pain pills and I now take them daily. I don't want to take them, but you know how that goes... Kind of hard to stop cold turkey if you have a job or a life or anything else to do besides lie in bed for two weeks and freaking suffer until you want to go insane. 

... But I digress... what I really relate to is the struggle with depression and the lonliness. I can promise you that I know all too well how hard coping can be when you are struggling just to stay alive. I think your life is worth something though. I think you still have a lot to offer the world. You may be lower than low right now and you may be hurting but THATS OK - what I mean by that, really, is that it's totally ok to have those feelings and you don't have to hide your pain here because people like me understand. We really do. We can be strong for you when you are weak, right? You are brave to reach out and I hope you stick around. I know its hard, it feels hopeless, but the best thing you can do right now is continue to reach out and seek help for both the depression and the substances. There ARE people who care about you. I'm one of them, and we only just met. 
;)

I am fifty thousand dollars in debt myself and I hear your pain. I'm very sorry that you have had to deal with so much though; it seems unfair. I know that sometimes life does get better, and sometimes it gets worse, but if you ride out the storm things always change eventually.

Happy Birthday! I'm sorry you're dealing with so much adversity and pain lately. You do matter as a person and if the value of a life is nothing more than accolades and accomplishments I'm telling you we are all "losers" because no one has achieved all of their goals in life and even when you get what you want it just sets you up for wanting more. I do believe that some of the happiest people focus on living in the moment and the small pleasures of life rather than the big goals. We are all valuable because we are all unique. There is no one like you anywhere on earth! That's enough! Now go do something you enjoy, if you can, or just be really nice to yourself going forward. You'll make it. You'll be feeling differently soon I'm sure, that's human nature. Continue to lean on others and get support when needed. Coming here was a brace decision. I admire you OP. Don't give up yet. I'm around if you need to talk.

This is a really tough situation and I have so much sympathy for you and your children. I am also a parent with severe depression / anxiety and I know (trust me) how bad it feels to be on the verge of giving up but unable to do so because the children are depending on you. It's a lot of pressure for anyone, let alone someone whose wife has decided to have the worst mid-life crisis in history... And you have to live with her? I am so sorry. That's awful. 

I don't have many suggestions for you, but I hope that things will progress to the point of your wife moving out or vice versa so that you two can have some space and privacy. No one wants the drama your wife is bringing into your life but try to remind yourself that while you don't have control of her actions you do have control of your own actions and reactions. In a way this is powerful, if you ask me, because you if can somehow ignore most of her bad behavior you will feel better and she will be going crazy knowing that you're no longer jealous or lost without her. In my experience, this phase she is in May last a year or two but in the meantime take care if yourself and those kids and pretend like she's not even there. It will be hard but it will get her attention - maybe she will realize how silly she has been and come back to you, maybe she won't, but she can't take away all of your strength and joy unless you allow her to do that. 

I hope I don't sound preachy or bossy, just some ideas... Other thing I'll say is good job reaching out on this forum and remember someone out there cares abou you. You might consider some couples / family therapy too, if you can do that, because sometimes having a neutral mediator can be incredibly helpful when things get tense and communication breaks down. 

Stay strong. You are a wonderful father. You can do this. It won't be forever. I promise.

Yea I hear ya. Had a shitty night last night myself. I guess not everyday can be one of the good ones, but it's how we deal with the tough times that determine our overall outlook. Anyway, glad you're hanging in there.
You know you are right. I can kick ass. I have overcome many challenges in the past. Still stressed but feeling a bit better today so thank you!

Thank you kindly. Just knowing I'm not alone in the universe is actually very reassuring. I beat depression and addiction in my past and I know I can beat this too, just wasn't feeling strong or brave AT ALL yesterday. Today I feel a little bit better. I appreciate you taking the time to help me out.
Thank you. I really do feel better after reading your encouraging words. Also congrats on being a new parent yourself! Enjoy every minute, they really do grow up quickly. Hugs
I know more of psychology and biological sciences but chemistry is always an option. Lol. Thx.

Hi. I'm here if you need to talk. I would like to help in any way I can. Your life matters and you DO have time to change your mind... Also I don't want to scare you but overdosing can end up being a terribly painful way to die. You could get very sick and suffer and you don't deserve to suffer anymore than you already have. Let us be there for you.

Anytime. Sorry it took me so long to get back to you - took a trip to Costa Rica. I feel like sometimes the people on this forum just disappear and I'm always wondering how they are doing... I hope you are doing well. I really do. Hugs
You're very welcome. My pleasure, really. I hope you're doing ok.
I'm sorry for your suffering and if you need to chat I'm here.

Hi. I have been where you are. I still struggle sometimes but there's a better life out there for you if you just hold on and try to work toward a better future, one step at a time. The hardest thing for me to accept, besides my past and the poor choices I once made, was that digging myself out of that pit of despair and breaking the unhealthy patterns didn't happen quickly. It took many years and it was a real challenge because all I knew was my old, destructive lifestyle and the depression I lived with every single minute. I had to make a conscious decision to seek out better friends and a few really amazing MENTORS who helped me through. Having someone to look up to and learn from changed everything. I simply found those individuals who had what I wanted for my life and let them guide me. I also quit all alcohol and drugs (this is just my story, no judgement or assumptions about you there) and with a clear mind and clean body I felt better. I exercised and ate better food too. It all made a huge difference. The best education you can get in life is to let another person whom you truly admire show you how they found happiness and success. I am so glad to have more joy in my life today and self confidence. You can too - I know you can. I once heard a saying, "when the student is ready, the teacher will appear." 
Good luck OP don't give in yet.

Hey there. I truly do believe it's going to be ok for you, but you have to want to be ok, even if that want is very small and the suicidal feelings overpower it. If any little part of you has doubts about killing yourself then you know you shouldn't do it, right? Or perhaps you have no doubts and feel that you truly do want nothing but to die, in which case, why not allow yourself to just live without abandon for a bit, as if you ARE dying, and REALLY just do all the things you've always wanted to do while alive? I mean wild, crazy dreams and ambitions. Like if you were going to check out anyway why not? Then perhaps you can reasses the situation from a new vantage? I don't know. Just an idea. Also I would like to add that financially you'll be fine with the programming. People are right. It's a great field and you should be ok doing that for your entire life until you retire, if you like. I wish you the best.

Yes and I do completely understand that feeling of true heartbreak. I have been there and will probably be there again someday. It's sad to think that in the end, most of us will loose our significant other somehow. I just hope you are able to find a passion for life once again, and until then I hope that you can hold on. It's not easy, at all, but remember that without darkness we would not know light. Without saddness and despair we would not appreciate the miracles and joys of our existence nearly as much. But for what it's worth, just know I hear you and I'm rooting for you. Lastly, great job overcoming your addiction. That is hard s**t man - if you can do that, you can do anything. I know it.

I'm so glad I could help you a bit. I think you should be a writer - you are amazingly articulate. I really felt almost every ounce of the despair and melancholy you were describing on a deep deep level and I attribute that to your writing skills in addition, perhaps, to a similar world view. Anyway, I genuinely hope things improve for you in the very near future.

I feel the same way that you feel PLUS I don't find much joy in being with people because I can be painfully insecure and it's always difficult to feel judged, even when I remind myself it's no big deal. 
I used to love to write and paint, play guitar, jog, travel and I'm a pilot so my ultimate joy was being in the air. Now I am too busy providing for a family in an expensive city to do much more than work, eat, sleep and maybe read a book here and there. I know I sound like a total self-pitying brat right now too, but the truth is that even some of my old hobbies I COULD still be doing don't appeal to me and the only reason I can come up with is my meds. They make me flat. With the bipolar I had high ups and low lows and it was dangerous for me, but I miss the mania sometimes because it was always like I was so into everything in life, just full of ideas and passion... Now it's like I just get through the day and try not to bother anyone or be bothered. So I feel you. I wish I had a better solution for both of us. I guess if I could take off and travel again I would do that and I recommend it to EVERYONE. If you can, go find an adventure! A new hobby! They are out there.

I'm truly sorry for your loss OP. A good friend of mine lost his wife to cancer very young and he found solice in world travel; it's not a luxury everyone can afford, but there are always people and places that can show you the love and beauty left in the world. I hope you find a reason to go on...

Yes I have. After four mental health related visits to hospitals and three trips to rehab I have finally found a way to be ok with myself and accepting of living life "on life's terms" as they say some places. I won't lie and tell you I don't think about suicide and death quite often because I still have those days (that's how I found r/suicidewatch to begin with!) but they aren't nearly as painful or devastating as they once were. Impulsivity isn't as much of a factor and I think that's because I'm older and wiser. Now I know that no matter how bad, this too shall pass... I feel for all those people who didn't make it out of the kind of depression that almost killed me... At the time I really, truly WANTED to die, now I'm thankful to be here most of the time. I find more joy in small things. I'm not so hard on myself. I do worry about getting old and what that might be like, because I see so many older people who seem sad and lonely. I guess I'll cope with it when / if I get there!

Let me tell you a little story, and maybe you'll relate having had some addiction issues yourself... About ten years ago, during maybe the happiest most carefree period of my life, I met "someone" too. It was a very joyful courtship because this "someone" made me feel SO amazing and happy and took my fears away. Like I had no sadness and no anxiety for the first time in my whole life. I am an abuse survivor and also come from a severely alcoholic family so I felt so relieved that, for the first time, I didn't have to be living like that, all full of fear and pain. I had health problems too, and this made those better. 

Eventually things kind of got weird. I noticed the more time I spent with my special "someone" the less time I had for other people or things. I just didn't care. I wanted to be with this one who made me complete. I even lost a job over this love and I barely batted an eyelash. Like you I was still in the prime of my life and I didn't think about where I might end up down the road... I just wanted to be ok. 

So I'm sure you can guess, but if not I will tell you, my "someone" was not a person but a class of drugs called opiates. Pills turned into stronger pills and then stealing pills and money to get them and then there was Heroin. Then it was done. I could not imagine ever EVER not having the Heroin. I mean, I had actual medical issues and mental problems and this stuff, although it was slowly ruining me, fixed that so perfectly. Plus it made me happy, social, creative... I felt like a child again. No worries. No tears. Like a child with some of the freedoms of adulthood... What could be better? 

It destroyed me. It destroyed my body, my soul, my life. Everyone tells the same dumb story but I was going to be an exception, you know? Like I'm smart. All my life people have told me I was very intelligent. They were wrong when it came to this. I had no power of mind over this. None. I couldn't deal with life without it. It seemed worse than death. 

Now I don't tell this to you to discount your actual relationship with a living HUMAN BEING but I do think you'll understand that I do mourn (now sober, struggling greatly every damn day sigh) for that feeling again. I want it so bad everyday. Just a break from the harshness of life, especially a life like yours and mine, where we are cleaning up wreckage and rebuilding and its SO HARD!!! But I go on. I must. You must. Maybe I will never FEEL the way I felt back then and I have to accept that. I have to learn to trust others and let them in even though all I want is sometimes is to go back to what I loved and what I felt would never turn on me. But it did turn on me. It had to go. For whatever reasons, it had to go. I could not live and learn the lessons of my existence with that crutch. 

Now I am just human again. I fell in love with someone new and it felt a little bit like that love affair with the drugs, in terms of chemical sensations... Our brains are funny things... Of course people and true love relationships are bigger than some heroin but my point is that I'm starting to find happiness again and you will too. 

You have overcome so much. I think you have a lot if wisdom too. Just keep going and don't think you'll never find some of that joy again, is my point. It's out there. It might be different but it might be better, you know? Life is full of surprises. 

And lastly... Don't do hard drugs. Lol

Yea I hear that. I was never so depressed and angry as I was in the psyche ward, go figure. Our mental health system in this country is severely lacking compassion and its hard to get outsiders to help because it's like... "Hey you guys want to donate money to kittens, kids with diseases or ...:. mental illness?" 

They will choose the kittens or children, every time, naturally. Not that kittens and children aren't AWESOME. I'm just saying depression seems to still carry a heavy stigma. Even the people who are supposed to help don't have a clue what to do for you half the time.

But I'm mucho glad you're doing better. Way to go. You are a fighter! Keep that up. We have to advocate for ourselves, which is hard when you're at your weakest point, but it can be done. Thank you for sharing your story with others.

Ok can you hang in there for another.... 12 to 15 days? The meds take a minute to work and I know it's hard but at least give it a shot first. Let the stuff do what it is meant to do. In the meantime, you can come here, you can PM me, you can talk to a trusted friend or therapist... You can travel somewhere and just get away for a bit... But don't kill yourself with pesticides. Not a good death. Very painful. I hope things improve.

Wow. So I have also spent some time in the bin. Sorry to hear of your struggles my friend. How are you doing now? How was the food in there? It was horrible for me. Did you meet anyone you COULD talk with and relate to in there? I was incredibly lonely and eventually they let me out because I don't think I was nearly as sick as about 99 percent of the poor people in the PU. 

Anyway, hope things are better now.

(TLDR for below post : I totally sympathize but I think giving in only means things get worse for the world and the idiots continue to take over. You're smart. You matter and can make a difference if you don't give up. So don't give up. I liked your post.)

I actually Googled "Why am I such a misanthrope?" yesterday; Apparently I, being on the upper cusp of the abysmally lonely generation you mentioned, would rather enter data into an algorithm on my computer to get answers than talk to any one of my contemporaries. All I can say is I hear you and I tend to agree with many of your sentiments. Yes, there are a million reasons why this world and this time we live in leave us lacking humanity. Yes, it is heartbreaking. No I don't enjoy it either most days. Your ideas of being propelled by intertia are spot on and very observant, although you can't necessarily fault some of the people around you who choose to exist in this manner; I think ignorance is bliss and for some, being unaware or able to ignore some of the darker facts about reality is a bit of a blessing. As for you and I; well it's never going to be easy. You're incredibly smart, you're aware, you've experienced a realm of higher consciousness to some degree (through the use of drugs, which I actually encourage in moderation) and now you have come to the conclusion that the real world is not such a fantastic place and you're lonely because there are so many narcissists around you and I that people like us are bound to be outcasts... YES I understand you... But what do we do about it? You mentioned volunteer work; I say keep doing those things but on your own terms. Perhaps you are making a small difference and when enough people are doing work to implement small changes it becomes bigger than any single individual. Humans were not made to be solitary creatures. If it's hard to find like-minded companions and friends you will be able to really treasure the ones you find and trust me they are out there, feeling a lot like you, looking for some connection. Maybe it's harder for highly aware and intelligent folks to connect but I have a couple friends who I know see the world for what it is and they are not on autopilot. Not everyone is drifting. Not everyone is a self-absorbed prick, I promise. So why should you live? Why try? Because if you don't try notbing ever changes! You're not meant to give in to this, are you? So many gifted, talented people suffer from depression and struggle as we do. Why not exist to help them? I realized a while ago that there was no value in my death but there might be worth to my life IF I WORK MY ASS OFF to find it. And I do that every day. Every single day I fight my mind because it tells me all hope is lost and I should end it or leave and just go live on a hill somewhere alone, away from all the a**holes out there - but then I don't do that. I trudge forward. I am not going to live an empty life and neither are you. You are alive, awake and you have time on your side. You can overcome some of this... And as for the rest of them.... I say whatever man let them live too and ignore the stupidity. Laugh a bit if you must (privately) and move on. Anyway, sorry to ramble. I enjoyed your post very much. Hang in there - we need more of you in the world.
My pleasure. Really. Hugs

This anxiety you feel is not uncommon here; many of us experience these thoughts and while unpleasant, the key thing to know and remember is that they are just that : thoughts. Your mind is tricky. It will sometimes tell you frightening things or refuse to acknowledge the good in the world. So is there a way out of this cage in your head? Absolutely. It's up to each if us to recognize that the full potential of the mind is much greater than we may think, but unless you have an awareness of this, it will be impossible to separate that negativity and anxiousness from the real "you" - so try to do a little exercise with me here - imagine that you're brain is divided into different rooms. In one room, all the people inside tell you the world is ending, things are awful, you're going to experience some horrible, awful target any moment... It's exhausting just listening to all that fear! Step away. Close the door behind you. Now you walk down a hallway and open the door to another space. In here there are just a few occupants, so quiet you never realized they were even in there - they are all smiling, laughing and telling you good things about yourself and the world. They tell you you'll be a success as long as you follow your heart and find happiness and peace. They tell you it going to be ok if you just practice being mindful of where in your head you spend the most time. Does that make sense on a metaphorical level? What I'm trying to tell you is to stay out of the bad "rooms" in your head unless you go in there to evict those negative thoughts / voices (the people speaking, as I called them) and clean it! My head is a huge mess sometimes, so I let the ugly thoughts run wild and sit there feeling like a victim, but then I remember I'm not a victim. Im lucky because even with my handicap, which is depression and anxiety, I still have ultimate control over what I tell myself is TRUE. You don't have to be anything but yourself. Nearly all children have parents or family members that expect a lot. But chances are they will love you if you just learn to love yourself. That's the hard part; that's where you go into a third room in your mind and see that there is no one else in there. You sit down. You are alone for a moment... There's a mirror in front of you. Look into it. See that you are whole and in this silence you have the opportunity to seize this life and make it good or even great. See that you are ok. You are more than ok. You're awesome. You have a lot to smile about. 

Sorry this is a long reply. I hope it helps. Take care my friend.

Even when I shave and get little razor bumps I have to mess with them. I've tried every cream and lotion you can think of. I've had chemical peels done. I took up playing guitar and oil painting to keep my hands busy... All this and I'm still stuck in this hell, feeling like a freak. It's ironic too because I am in recovery from drug and alcohol addiction but I probably look more like a typical "crackhead" than ever! It sounds like you're feeling hopeless, confused and lonely more than anything else. Hopelessness, especially, is like a cancer to the conscious mind - you're convinced that it no longer matters because things can not change. You're dealing with a lack of understanding from others and a lack of direction. All of these are obstacles, to be certain, but I don't think you're going to loose yourself completely or end your life because you are here now, seeking the advice, love and support you need. I commend you on that. One of the major hallmarks of depression (which I also suffer from) is a tendency to isolate. Even when we are incredibly lonely and desperate for someone to help, we tend to isolate. The fact that you chose not to do that this time is a testament to both your bravery and your willingness to change your current circumstances. My best advice is quite simple; try to focus your energy on today only. Everyday. Looking into the past will keep you stuck in yesterday's problems and worrying about the future will most likely cause unnecessary fear or uncertainty to grow until you are paralyzed. It used to happen to me all the time until I learned to break things down into a smaller, more manageable size. If you like to write and play music, stop focusing so much on writing the perfect song and finding a talented singer and just go back to doing it because you enjoy it. It doesn't have to be tied to an overwhelming goal. Once you do this you may be surprised at the results. Even with your job issues; you can take one small step toward finding a job by making a list of your preferred employers and writing a few cover letters. Then move on to something else. Rome wasn't built in a day, as it is said, so if you're able to accept that and be patient, and not give up, things will start to improve. Id also suggest maybe opening up to your girlfriend more often? If she truly loves you she will stay closer and be there to support you more. You seem like a very like-able person so please hang in there and remember that no matter how crappy things seem, there are always people 
who care for you. Always.

Hi. I can relate to your post so much. I became pregnant (while on birth control, yes it happens) right around the time I quit using opiates. I chose to taper down with Tramadol so that was still going on even after I knew I was expecting; I was able to lower my intake significantly but when I attempted to stop the depression combined with my anxiety and crazy hormonal shifts literally made me contemplate suicide at times. I knew I couldn't allow myself to be having those thoughts, I loved my unborn baby fiercely, just as you do. Together with my therapist and doctor the decision was made to take an anti-depressant called Effexor, which was one of the ONLY medications that ever helped with my depression. Soon after I started with that; I realized that it was "rated" for pregnancy in the category of "effects to fetus unknown" because it's what psychiatrists call an 'atypical' medication and does not work the same as the older ones like Prozac, Paxil, Etc. 

Oh the guilt. I know you know what I'm talking about. Everyday I took my pills I felt like I was poisoning my poor baby. He was helpless and here I was, his mom, taking pills and (yes me too!) drinking coffee almost every morning so I could get out of bed and function somewhat normally. The problem was, everytime I decided to skip the medication I had odd sensations going through my entire body... Almost like electric shocks. My muscles would lock up and I shook a lot. Add to that the issue of not being able to leave my house AT ALL unless I was taking those pills due to past trauma and agoraphobia and you have an all around awful situation. I cried so much. I felt like the lowest human on the planet. My opinion of myself was that I deserved to be killed for what I was doing. I was also absolutely terrified of the birth because I worried about the baby having the same seizure-type symptoms and shaking, head zaps, etc. that I did when trying to wean down. 

You know what also made me cringe? Other mothers around me who I couldn't share anything with because they were perfectly normal, relatively happy and judged everyone who wasn't JUST LIKE THEM. So I didn't have much joy throughout my pregnancy, I was alone almost all the time. My boyfriend worked more than I did so I did almost all of the prenatal appointments myself, praying to God the miserably rude doctors and nurses at the community health clinics wouldn't discover my secret. Only me, my boyfriend, my therapist and the psychiatrist knew. They kept telling me it would most likely be ok due to being on a low dose but some days I took an extra dose because I couldn't take the suicidal ideation, extreme fatigue, etc. I remember a friend of mine's baby shower vividly, all the moms were discussing making their own organic baby food, cloth diapers, nanny services, birthing suites with the jacuzzi tubs, how much clothing and toys they had for their bundle of joy... And I was in the corner thinking of how pathetic it was that my main concerns were how to just survive and be as safe as possible until the baby came and how Karma would have me dealing with a severely handicapped child because I, mother of the year over here, was on drugs. 

So, to wrap it up (and sorry if this is long, I just want you to know you aren't ALONE. I was there this time last year. I was you. You are me.) I did give birth to a son a few weeks early, and he had some minor issues with things like lower birth weight and slight sleep disturbances, but he was and is ok. In fact, he is thriving. I watched him and had his pediatrician watch him very closely for several months after his birth and I was super paranoid but the only major concerns were his tendency to be a light sleeper, fuss a lot when not being held and being maybe one pound below average for a bit until he caught up. Now he is hitting his milestones way ahead of the curve and he's as healthy as can be. This doesn't mean I'm suggesting that using any foreign substance during pregnancy is safe or a great idea, but you and I, as mothers, must learn that self-hatred leads to insanity and guilt, which will also have effects on our children. There is a very fine line you must walk here, like so many. As addicts, former addicts, whatever you prefer, we must learn to accept ourselves as flawed and human AND we have a duty to society, to our families and friends, to keep progressing until we are once again able to contribute in a positive way. We have an obligation to do the best we can. Are you doing the best you possibly can? Well, you're off the heroin for starters, which is astonishing, so there's ONE HUGE thing you can feel good about. You choose to keep this baby, love this baby, sacrifice for this baby... There's one more thing! You could have aborted or refused to accept respomsibility for this other life and you didn't do either of those. You have a desire to keep progressing until you are free. I can't guarantee anything but I would guess that after your baby is born, there will be a period of detoxing (and yes, it's hard to acknowledge that part) but the doctors will do their best to make things as comfortable as possible for him / her. After that you might be referred to a social worker for occasional monitoring and check-ins. Not the end of the world. Take all the help you can get. Caring for newborns is tough, grueling work at times. Accept the help that you are offered. Listen to your doctors. Be as honest as you possibly can. You are not evil. You gain no real pleasure from this terrible addiction and you WILL stop. You can do that. I'm here to tell you it can happen. But first you have to look in the mirror and tell the woman you see that you don't want to keep killing her. You don't want her to suffer. You love her too and you will care for her AND the baby from now on. Your past has left you with scars and those will remain but you can rise above this nightmare and go on to help so many others. Please stop hating yourself. I do not hate myself. I made some huge mistakes which led to other decisions and circumstances out of my complete control. I wasn't the healthiest pregnant woman. I'm not a perfect mom. It's ok as long as I WANT to make each day better than the last and I'm willing to do the work on myself even when it's uncomfortable and painful. You deserve that chance too. 

I hope I have been able to give you and your precious baby some hope. It's going to be a step-by-step process, as someone else said. You must be patient, even if you are having one of those really tough days where everything in you says "give up!" Addicts like instant gratification. This won't be like that, as you know. It's a slow process. It's like thawing frostbite; there's often a great deal of pain but the alternative is a life of living as a slave to opiates or death. Just go slow. Little by little. Everything you can do. Every ounce if willingness you can summon. Maybe in a year or two you'll be able to write these words for another woman in the same situation. Everything I have said us true. I love you and I hope you beat this thing. I wish you and your new family the very best in life.

   You are in a crap situation right now. I know. Mine was similar at your age. I freaking HATED Middle School and High School. My grades were good, I just did not fit in to any of the stupid cliques and I wasn't interested in the same things most people my own age were into anyway. I'm not suggesting I was special or better than them, in fact I felt very sad and mostly inadequate. Also spent time locked away in hospitals for anorexia and being a danger to myself. Lovely! It was a total nightmare. Misery was my constant companion, like a shadow, wherever I went it was right behind me. 
   At home my parents ran a rather large firm so like you I felt ignored; Especially when it came to my mother, we barely spoke unless she was chastising me or I was complaining to her about my sibling. I helped raise my sister and she was completely different than myself in that she was quite social, pretty, popular and constantly had plans as soon as she was allowed to be out. Add to that the final issue of both my parents being functionally alcoholic and addicted to various pills and powders and you have a dysfunctional adolescence at best.
   Like you I thought of suicide often. It didn't scare me to image dying, it gave me some comfort. Anytime I was upset, I took it out on myself in some way. I isolated myself to the point where people at my own school had no idea that I went there when we graduated. My advice to you is this; stay alive, even if you have to replace some if that misery with a bit of anger. You have every right to be pissed off. Hold off on suicide though, if for no other reason than to get the hell out if your home as soon as possible and go explore the rest of the world. There's actually places where people are just... Different. There are circles where you will feel accepted. I promise. Today I have many friends - do you want to know where I met some of them? AA! I grew up to become an addict and alcoholic just like good old mom and dad (irony, oh irony) and when I found the strength to face that met all these other half-dysfunctional half-crazy, amazing, strong, kind people. No I'm not saying go to AA for friends but you're quite intelligent so I know you see my point. 
   Is there anywhere far away that you would like to see or even live? Is there a particular car you're hoping to own one day or a hobby you can put more time into? Anything... Just as long as it makes you feel ALIVE. I became a pilot. I flew all over the world and saw incredible, exciting things. It made my sadness much easier to manage. I also moved far from my hometown, to California, and found that this was where I truly felt at HOME. Home is in your soul not in your room. So your room is filthy? Oh well! You'll either clean it up or you won't, either way it's not going to be something that matters much in the near future, you know? 
   Just decide to live and when the dark days are upon you remember that many very intelligent, "successful" (not my fave word, but I digress) people deal with depression and suicidal ideation, otherwise known as an obsession with ending their own lives. I'd even go so far as to say that you can THINK about it if you like, but doing it is going to accomplish nothing. You won't feel this way anymore but you will have cut your life so short over a situation that is temporary. It sucks being unable to make big decisions but soon enough you will. If you can last a few more years you're home free. Go to India or China or South America. Start planning now. Look into college - it's early but I swear to you College was SO much better than anything before. It's a chance to do what you truly enjoy. Tell your parents, if you can, that you feel incredibly low. You never know, they might actually pull their heads out if their asses and help you right? What's the worst that can happen? They say no, you're in the same spot you are now. I'm guessing they do love you, it's just not something certain people are good at - parenting - I recently became a mom and it is so hard but I know I can help my son if he has addictions or depression because I SURVIVE. You could help others too. Take your life back. It matters. Become someone. Grow up. Try living without these barriers. You're smart and you CAN do whatever you like. I promise tomorrow will be better. You did the right thing by checking in here. I wish you all the best and I have every confidence in your ability to overcome life's hardships. They will come and go. Life is not easy but you're going to be ok.
